title: Bodybuilding Basics: Learn form, Effort, and Progression
author: Aidan W.
desc: The purpose of this program is to ease you into lifting with low frequency, low volume, and high effort training. In these 4 weeks, you will gain a better understanding of how to perform basic functions like a press, a squat, a hip hinge, and a row. The program progresses linearly, meaning you will start at a low rep count until you can take that same weight to a higher rep count, then you will increase weight and restart that cycle. Each week you will focus on one thing: doing better than you did last week. That's it. Utilize the tutorials provided by boostcamp and the notes I've left to succeed in getting bigger, stronger and better. This program lasts for 1 month and should be performed while in some sort of calorie surplus, though a sufficient protein intake is a great place to start if you don't wish to track calories. Have fun, be patient with yourself and enjoy the process!

ex.note: Heavy hip-hinge movement. Focus on keeping weight close to shins and shifting hips back and forth to lower and raise weight. Pause at the bottom for a deep stretch in the hamstring.

Heavy squat movement. Keep feet close and low on the pad to get a deep stretch in quads at the bottom. Go as deep as possible, well past a 90° knee bend. Good pause at bottom. Keep whole foot planted.
Lean forward to keep a deep stretch in hamstring. Good pause at top to feel stretch.
Keep knee close to pad to avoid pain. Full stretch at bottom with a short pause.
Can be performed on leg Press, standing on a plate, or on machine. Look for a deep stretch at the bottom of each rep. Straight knee.
Raise bench by only 1 notch. Tuck elbows until your wrists are at a 45° rotation from vertical. Slow control lower until dumbells touch shoulders. Follow with a pause and press. Do not touch at top.
Set seat to where you hands grab handles at a point below shoulder level. Sit slightly forward on seat. Let elbows bend during stretch, then straighten arms when squeezing foreward.
Set up csble as shown in video. Keep elbows high and in place.
Normal bicep Curl, except wrists, are now vertical to work more of the forearm. Treat these as a primer to the other curls. Take these heavy and allow yourself to cheat just a little.
Keep chest high and elbows locked in place at your sides. Palms facing up, though you can twist wrists from neutral to face-up during Curl if you prefer.
similar to the dumbell press from last time. Raise seat until it is at a 45° angle or slightly higher. Use knees to kick dumbells into start position. Punch up, slow lowering until touching shoulders
Single arm cable side raise. Set cable to be just below hip-height. Straight arm, brace with off-hand on cable. Raise to the side at a comfortable angle.
Both Arms at once. Use light dumbells and keep arms straight. Raise to the side, as if T-posing, except the arms are brought in ~30° on each side to help shoulder joint.
Light dumbells. Performed these Bent over, holding the dumbells with thumbs pointed towards the floor. Fly behind you as if you wanted to elbow something behind your back.
Perform either on T-bar rowing machine, cable row, or machine row. Whatever lets you get a wide grip. Keep elbows as long as its comfortable, and drive them behind you.
Shoulder width or slightly wider grip. Slight lean backward. Focus on tucking elbows and driving them towards your pockets. Full stretch at top.
